one_liner: Graph database platform (self-managed or Aura cloud) with an Aura management API for provisioning instances and a Cypher query interface.

auth.evidence_quote: Authentication to the token endpoint uses HTTP Basic Authentication, where the client ID and client secret are provided as the username and password, respectively.
auth.notes: This covers the Aura management/control-plane API (client-credentials OAuth2). The actual database query interface (Bolt/Cypher) uses username/password or bearer auth per-driver, separate from the Aura API; database-level auth not re-verified this pass.

access.evidence_quote: API credentials are linked to the user account, inheriting its capabilities and roles.
access.notes: Aura has a free tier (AuraDB Free) and API credential creation is self-serve, per earlier search results ('All tiers can create Aura API credentials'), though that specific sentence wasn't fetched verbatim from the live page this pass.

api.evidence_quote: Neo4j Labs Model Context Protocol servers
api.notes: Aura control-plane API (instance/project management) is narrow in endpoint count. Two MCP options exist: neo4j/mcp (vendor org, official, local binary) and neo4j-contrib/mcp-neo4j (Neo4j Labs, community/experimental) -- classified official since neo4j/mcp is published under the vendor's own GitHub org.

verdict.rationale: Free Aura tier, self-serve OAuth2 client-credential API access, and an official MCP server support building now for instance management; database queries need separate driver-level credentials.
